title: For $415k, you can live in a New England community library
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: The former Tyler Free Library in Foster, Rhode Island, built in 1850, is on sale for $415,000.
Originally a schoolhouse, the 1,760-square-foot property includes a fireplace, hardwood floors, and a basement.
The building is zoned for agricultural/residential use but does not include the library's book collection in the sale.

title: Patriots 53-man roster projection 1.0: Will New England really stick with 7 receivers?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: New England Patriots' 53-man roster includes three quarterbacks: Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito, and Behren Morton.
Kayshon Boutte's status remains uncertain as Patriots could cut receiver group to six by trading or keeping him.
Patriots have eight wide receivers in contention, with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, and Mack Hollins as likely locks.

title: Adley Rutschman could make his Red Sox debut in coming days
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman could debut for the Red Sox in Toronto after recovering from wrist inflammation.
The catcher joined Boston after a trade with Baltimore and played two rehab games with Triple-A Worcester.
Rutschman's activation adds depth to the Red Sox amid their recent series loss to the Athletics.

title: Healey signs bill allowing state to take Norwood Hospital through eminent domain
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Governor Maura Healey signed a bill allowing the state to seize Norwood Hospital via eminent domain as of November 1.
The 11-acre Norwood Hospital property has been idle since 2020 due to flood damage and bankruptcy of Steward Health Care.
Medical Properties Trust, the current owner, claims to have invested $350 million and advocates completing the construction themselves.

title: Dozens displaced by building collapse in Springfield
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A building collapse at 265 Dwight St. Ext. in Springfield displaced 45 people without injury, following severe thunderstorms.
Mayor Domenic J. Sarno declared a state of emergency due to power outages and downed trees from the storms.
The Red Cross and Eversource crews are assisting displaced residents and addressing power outages in Springfield.

title: Adam Vinatieri jokes about Bill Belichick, Deflategate as part of Hall-of-Fame speech
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adam Vinatieri was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, reflecting on his 24-year NFL career.
During his speech, Vinatieri joked about Bill Belichick's absence and the Patriots' Deflategate controversy.
Vinatieri expressed gratitude to Patriots fans and teammates, praising their role in the team's success.

title: Mass. 7-year-old hit and killed by vehicle while riding bike
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 7-year-old was struck and killed by a vehicle while biking in Williamstown, Massachusetts, on Friday.
The collision occurred at the intersection of Main Street and Buxton Hill Road around 5:40 p.m., officials reported.
No arrests or charges have been made; the driver was not impaired, and the investigation is ongoing.

title: Residents urged to keep pets out of Stoughton pond after dog’s death
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Stoughton officials warn residents to keep pets out of Ames Pond after a dog's death potentially linked to algae.
Algae blooms, which may be present in Ames Pond, can cause illnesses in humans and be fatal to animals.
Weekly E. Coli tests at Ames Pond meet state safety requirements, but cyanobacterial blooms remain a concern.

title: Former NH state trooper decertified after misleading police about using GPS to track girlfriend
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: James Lamoureux, former NH State Trooper, decertified for misleading police about GPS tracking his girlfriend.
Lamoureux pleaded guilty to false reports, resulting in a suspended six-month prison sentence, deferred for two years.
He has resigned from the force and will be on a national registry, barring future law enforcement employment.

title: Man polishing powder horn outside Lexington church prompts bizarre police response
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Lexington police responded to Grace Chapel on a report of a man with a gun, prompting a building lockdown.
The man was found to be polishing a musket-era powder horn, part of his hobby as a reenactor, posing no threat.
Heavy police presence led to parts of Worthen Road closing, but police confirmed no danger to the public.
